title: Encode binary data directly into Base64 buffers
goal: Round-trip binary payloads as standard padded Base64 characters or UTF-8 while retaining buffer and final-block contracts.

selectionNotes: Uses standard padded Base64, not Base64Url. Preserve unconsumed tails; RC2 TryDecodeFromChars can throw for malformed text.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This edition uses .NET 11 library APIs; the .NET 10 code is a comparison, not a catalogue route.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 sample with the .NET 11 SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical net11.0 project selects the .NET 11 default C# 15 language mode.

prerequisites: Use a net11.0 console project with LangVersion=15.0. Include the imports stated in the recipe.
constraints: This is standard Base64, not Base64Url: alphabet and padding differ. Use GetEncodedLength/GetMaxDecodedLength for destination planning, and consume only the written portion. The OperationStatus forms preserve consumed/written and isFinalBlock semantics; retain unconsumed tails across blocks. The test proves a non-final two-byte tail returns NeedMoreData with zero consumption. In the actual RC2 artifact TryDecodeFromChars throws FormatException for malformed text; Try here is not a blanket promise of nonthrowing validation. Use the OperationStatus overload for InvalidData. A short destination is a separate condition. Encoding does not encrypt, authenticate or compress the payload.
stabilityLimitations: RC2 verification; GA reconciliation remains pending.
